identity.name: Karaya gum
identity.chemical_class: Natural acidic polysaccharide hydrocolloid (plant exudate gum from Sterculia species)

function.mechanism: Swells in water to form a viscous hydrocolloid network that thickens/stabilizes foods; largely not digested and can act as a mechanical bulk laxative at high intake.

adi.basis: EFSA (2016 re-evaluation) concluded no need for a numerical ADI for E416 and no safety concern at refined exposure for reported uses/use levels.

efsa.key_finding: No concern for genotoxicity; no adverse effects in carcinogenicity studies at highest tested doses; no safety concern for general population at refined exposure, while adults should avoid intakes above about 7000 mg/person/day due to abdominal discomfort.

adi.basis: JECFA latest evaluation lists ADI as NOT SPECIFIED.

concerns.summary: Historical human reports in JECFA documentation describe inhalation/oral hypersensitivity to karaya gum (asthma, dermatitis, gastrointestinal symptoms) in susceptible individuals.

Gastrointestinal intolerance can occur at high bolus intake; EFSA notes abdominal discomfort around 7000 mg/person/day in adults. Case reports describe esophageal bezoar with laxative granules and a non-food Sterculia-related liver injury case.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA re-evaluation: no need for numerical ADI and no safety concern for general population at refined exposure
JECFA monograph: high dietary-level animal studies did not indicate meaningful toxicity
JECFA mutagenicity section: no consistent mutagenic signal in reviewed assays

adi_exceedance.notes: Numerical ADI exceedance is not directly applicable because EFSA uses a non-numerical ADI approach and JECFA ADI is not specified.

risk_assessment.rationale: Major regulators converge on low concern at authorized food-use levels (EU approved with no numerical ADI, US CFR Part 184 GRAS framework, JECFA ADI not specified). Residual concern is mainly limited to high-dose gastrointestinal intolerance and historical hypersensitivity in susceptible individuals.
key_factors: EFSA 2016: no need for numerical ADI and no safety concern at refined exposure
21 CFR 184.1349 provides GRAS-framework listing with explicit use limits
JECFA latest evaluation (1988): ADI not specified
No IARC monograph classification entry found for karaya gum
Case-level/older signals exist for allergy and high-dose GI effects
